expounded

/ik-SPOWN-did/ - the stress falls on SPOWN; the recording says the base form, expound · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Expounded means explained something in careful detail.

Invite Grandpa to explain the tides and settle in: he once expounded on moon phases straight through dessert.

Example

Ask the bookshop owner whether first editions matter and pull up a stool. Last Tuesday she expounded on paper stocks, binding glue, and the scandal of a certain 1922 print run for forty unbroken minutes, pausing only to sell a birthday card.

Expounded is the exact verb because it means explained something in careful detail — she is not summarizing; she is setting the whole subject out, piece by labeled piece. Elucidate promises the fog will lift; expounded promises thoroughness, and it may outlast your afternoon.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

held forth: To have held forth is to have talked long and enthusiastically, invited or not — the phrase measures the talker's momentum, not the listener's gain. Expounded promises that the length served the subject: a topic laid out in careful, ordered detail, piece by piece.

spelled out: Spelled out means made every step explicit so nothing can be misread, and it can be done in three short lines. Expounded adds sheer fullness: the speaker goes long on purpose, covering the whole subject and not just the steps someone might trip over.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

glossed over: hurried past with the thinnest possible mention

condensed: packed the matter into fewer words

Where it sits · how fully the subject gets covered — mentioned → sketched → expounded

mentioned vs. expounded: Mentioned is the smallest coin next to expounded — the subject gets named once and the conversation moves on, where to have expounded is to have stayed and covered it all.

sketched vs. expounded: Sketched stops short of expounded — an outline in a few strokes, where to have expounded is to have filled in every panel of the picture.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out

Root — pound

Root — pound: to put, to place (Latin ponere, worn smooth in English)

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: past-tense ending

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- (out) + pound (to place) + -ed (past tense) = 'set out in the open.' Latin ponere, 'to put,' hides as -pound in several English verbs — a compound is things placed together, and to propound is to put an idea forward. To have expounded a subject is to have taken it out of its box and placed every part on the table.

Use the root in a new word: component

Use the root in a new word: component: The technician swapped out one faulty component, and the whole console came back to life.

Word Choice

formal / bookish

Expounded says the speaker went long on purpose, laying a subject out in full. If the audience just needed the fog cleared, elucidate; if they needed it shorter, this unit's summarize was the job. Expounded is neutral-to-wry — the detail is loving, whether or not anyone asked for all of it.
